newsitem.title: UK: Russian Geoilbent oil JV gets $55 mln EBRD loan.
newsitem.headline: Russian Geoilbent oil JV gets $55 mln EBRD loan.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) said on Thursday it was providing a $55 million loan to Russian joint venture Geoilbent Ltd to develop western Siberian oilfields.

In a statement, the EBRD said the loan, which has a maximum term of eight years, would be used to ensure the continued commercial development of the North Gubkinskoye and Priskonovoye oil and gas fields in western Siberia.

The fields have total estimated recoverable reserves of 300 million barrels of crude. As part of an overall $329 million development programme, more than 300 new wells will be drilled and production facilities and infrastructure will be expanded to meet increased production rates.
"The development of these fields represents an additional step towards arresting the decline of Russia's oil production," said Ron Freeman, first vice president of the EBRD.
Output of the Geoilbent venture is expected to peak at 75,000 barrels per day (bpd) from 8,000 bpd now.
Geoilbent was established in 1991 by Russian companies Purneftegas and Purneftegasgeologia, both owning 33 percent, and Benton Oil and Gas Co of the United States which holds 34 percent.

The EBRD has structured the project on the value of the company's reserves using so-called "borrowing-base" non-recourse financing, said Sergey Popov, co-director of the EBRD's natural resources team.
"This is the first time such an innovative approach has been used in Russia," Popov said.
